phase_name: Demonstrate the Closed Loop End to End

objectives.description: Stage a fixture task with modified_files under agent-system/extensions/** outside the allowlist
Drive through the four-move loop with a stale deployed tree, capture exit-6 refusal
Capture cycle_modified_files non-empty, deploy_pending:true, checkpoint firing next cycle
Confirm no fresh implement dispatch against an already-complete plan
Record evidence in the task summary artifact

phase_notes:
Built a scripted, real-script demonstration (not a mock of the logic under test): an isolated mktemp -d fixture repo with the REAL orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, update-task-status.sh, skill-base.sh, and their full dependency chain copied in unmodified, driven through four steps. Full transcript saved at progress/phase-4-demonstration-transcript.txt (durable evidence artifact). Summary:

Step 1 (cycle N postflight): fixture candidate #8801 (task_type meta, modified_files=["agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/some_other_file.sh"] -- deliberately NOT one of orchestrator-critical-paths.json's curated entries) resolves an implement dispatch against a deliberately stale .claude-extensions.json. update-task-status.sh's PHASE 0.5 gate refuses with exit 6 (verbatim message matching the live incident). Phase 2's honesty fix produces verdict=defer and the 'orchestration paused (cycle 0)' commit -- not 'complete implementation'. Phase 1's accumulation guarantee holds: cycle_modified_files is non-empty afterward. skill-base.sh's pre-existing (now finally consumed) machinery records deploy_pending:true on .return-meta.json.

Step 2 (cycle N+1 orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh): Phase 3's widened predicate fires the Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint even though 0 critical paths matched the curated allowlist, naming its own reason (the deploy_pending marker) rather than the old misleading 'touched 0 orchestrator-critical path(s)' line. The (stubbed, but behaviorally realistic -- it syncs the recorded source_git_head to the fixture source repo's actual HEAD) deploy-headless.sh runs; verify-deploy.sh reports clean; cycle_modified_files resets to []. A fresh implement dispatch IS prepared this cycle -- this is the plan's own named, accepted one-cycle-deferred-convergence cost, not a defect: the task is still genuinely 'implementing' since the prior write was refused.

Step 3 (cycle N+1 postflight retry): re-running postflight for the same candidate (modelling the re-dispatched agent's own return, which a real general-implementation-agent would produce immediately since all plan phases are already [COMPLETED] -- see its own Stage 3 early-return contract) now succeeds: [deploy-check] finds the extension fresh, verdict=ok, state.json -> completed, 'complete implementation' commit. NO manual deploy-headless.sh run and NO manual reconcile-task-status.sh replay occurred anywhere in the transcript -- both convergence steps were fully automated.

Step 4 (subsequent cycle-plan call): dispatch[] is empty, stop.reason=all_terminal -- confirming the previously-observed live failure mode (a fresh implement dispatch prepared against an already-4/4-complete plan) does not recur once the task reaches completed.

Acceptance #5 (no test weakened/deleted): verified via `git diff <pre-task-commit> HEAD -- <the three test files>` -- the only removed lines across all three phases' commits combined are two `for f in ...; do` loop-header lines in test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's setup_sandbox, replaced with an identical line plus `deploy-freshness-lib.sh` appended to the file list (a loop-list extension, not a removed assertion). No `pass`/`fail` assertion, no test case, and no comparison was removed or loosened anywhere.
